item.title: New Break seeks $550,000 to fund drilling at its Timmins-area gold project
item.description: The flow-through financing would fund exploration spending at the company's Moray project, 49 kilometres southeast of Timmins, Ontario, if it closes as planned.
item.content:encoded: New Break Resources Ltd. (CSE: NBRK) said October 30 that it intends to complete a non-brokered private placement of up to 2,500,000 flow-through common shares at $0.22 per share, for gross proceeds of up to $550,000. The company expects the offering to close within the next two business days, subject to acceptance by the Canadian Securities Exchange and other customary conditions. The shares qualify as flow-through shares within the meaning of subsection 66(15) of the Income Tax Act (Canada). New Break said the proceeds will be used for Canadian Exploration Expenses, which it will renounce to the purchasers of the shares with an effective date of no later than December 31, 2026, as stated in the release. The company said the proceeds raised through the offering will go toward ongoing drilling at its Moray gold project, located 49 kilometres southeast of Timmins, Ontario, in the Abitibi greenstone belt. The release gave no drill results or further technical detail on the current program. Qualified finders who introduce subscribers to the offering may receive a cash fee equal to 6% of the proceeds from those subscribers, plus finder's warrants equal to 6% of the flow-through shares sold to them, exercisable at $0.22 per share for 24 months from closing, according to the release. All securities issued under the offering, including any finder's warrants, are subject to a statutory hold period of four months and one day from the date of issuance, the standard resale restriction under Canadian securities law for this type of exemption. New Break describes itself as a Canadian mineral exploration company focused primarily on the Moray project, and also holds a 20% carried interest in the Sundog gold project in Nunavut. The release did not disclose the size of New Break's partner's interest in Sundog or any other terms of that arrangement.

item.title: A Southeast Asian conglomerate still awaits one approval for Altura's $3-million raise
item.description: Altura Energy extended the deadline to close its $3-million helium financing to November 30 while its investor's bank sign-off is pending.
item.content:encoded: Altura Energy Corp. (TSXV: ALTU) said October 30 that it has extended, to November 30, 2026, the deadline to complete a non-brokered private placement of 18,541,400 units at $0.1618 each, for gross proceeds of C$3 million. The TSX Venture Exchange has granted conditional acceptance of the offering, which the company first disclosed in a July 28, 2026 news release. Each unit under the offering comprises one common share and one share purchase warrant, exercisable at $0.25 for 36 months from the closing date. A non-brokered placement is one an issuer sells directly to subscribers rather than through an investment dealer, which is consistent with the release naming no agent or underwriter on the transaction. The sole subscriber is described in the release only as a leading Southeast Asian conglomerate; Altura's release does not name the investor. That investor has obtained approval from its own local Ministry of Finance to proceed, but the release said it is still awaiting a further approval from its state bank before the financing can close. Altura said the investor will have the right to nominate one member to the board of directors once the placement completes; the release did not disclose who might be nominated or any further governance terms attached to the investment beyond that right. The extension is the only change disclosed in the October 30 release; the unit count, the per-unit price and the warrant terms are unchanged from the July 28 announcement, according to the company. No new closing date beyond November 30, 2026, was given, and the release did not say what happens if that date passes without the state bank's approval. Altura describes itself as a helium-focused exploration company advancing prospects in the Holbrook Basin of Arizona, targeting helium for uses the company lists as healthcare, semiconductors, aerospace and other advanced-technology applications. The company also trades on the OTCQB under the symbol ALTUF and on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange under Y020.

item.title: Edgewater Wireless settles debenture interest in shares, including some to its own directors
item.description: The TSX Venture company will issue 1,421,982 shares at $0.05 to cover $71,100 in interest owed on debentures issued in 2022.
item.content:encoded: Edgewater Wireless Systems Inc. (TSXV: YFI) said October 30 that it will settle an aggregate of $71,100.01 owed in interest on its unsecured debentures, issued September 1, 2022, by issuing 1,421,982 common shares at a deemed price of $0.05 per share. The interest covers four quarterly obligations dated December 1, 2025, March 1, 2026, June 1, 2026 and September 1, 2026. Of the shares being issued, 265,995 are going to company directors, the release said. Edgewater said that participation triggers the related-party transaction requirements of Multilateral Instrument 61-101, which governs transactions between an issuer and its insiders. Edgewater said it qualifies for an exemption from the formal-valuation and minority-shareholder-approval requirements that would otherwise apply, because neither the fair value of the shares nor the debt being settled exceeds 25% of the company's market capitalization, as calculated under the instrument. The debt settlement remains subject to the approval of the TSX Venture Exchange, the company said. The release did not state when that approval is expected or what happens to the arrangement if it is not granted. Separately, Edgewater said it granted 900,000 stock options to employees and consultants at an exercise price of $0.05 per share. The options expire five years from the date of grant, according to the release. Edgewater also trades over the counter in the United States under the symbol KPIFF. The release gave no further detail on the company's current financial position or on why the interest was settled in shares rather than cash.

item.title: OpenAI cuts its funding target by $10 billion as AI stocks slide
item.description: The ChatGPT maker now seeks $20 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation, down from a $30 billion target.
item.content:encoded: OpenAI has cut the target for its latest funding round by $10 billion, now seeking about $20 billion rather than the $30 billion it had been pursuing, according to a Financial Times report carried by Reuters. The company is also seeking a lower valuation, $1.25 trillion rather than the $1.4 trillion target. OpenAI had set a Friday deadline for investor commitments, Reuters reported. The reduction follows a selloff across technology stocks tied to concerns over the scale of AI infrastructure spending. Reuters reported the Nasdaq fell 2.9% on the day the cut was reported and is down 7.8% from its October 6 peak. Some investors have reduced the size of their commitments to the round, and the fund's 'first close' — the initial tranche of capital committed — is expected to come in below the revised $20 billion target. Reuters named several participants in the round, including the UAE-backed technology fund MGX, expected to be the largest investor, alongside Founders Fund, Coatue, Sequoia Capital and Andreessen Horowitz. OpenAI is pursuing a public listing in 2027, and Reuters reported the company had been keen to close this round ahead of rival Anthropic's anticipated listing, since the two companies draw on an overlapping investor base. The theme comprises 29 listed venture names; 18 traded today, 5 higher and 9 lower, for a median move of -2.17% against -2.77% for the S&P/TSX Venture Composite. The spread between the two was 0.60 percentage points. Perimeter Medical Imaging Ai In (TSXV: PINK) rose 28.57% to CAD0.18, and is in the theme because its registered name contains "ai." Sparc AI Inc. (CSE: SPAI) fell 8.77% to CAD2.08, and is in the theme because its registered name contains "ai." Railtown AI Technologies Inc (CSE: RAIL) rose 1.72% to CAD0.295, and is in the theme because its registered name contains "ai." OpenAI's funding news and these moves fell on the same trading day. Nothing in the public record ties the two together: the theme's -2.17% median move and the Composite's -2.77% decline are both simply what the board did that day.

item.title: Ashley Gold closes C$2.08-million private placement in two tranches
item.description: The final tranche raised C$631,275 at 6.5 and 8 cents a unit, pending Canadian Securities Exchange acceptance of the full offering.
item.content:encoded: Ashley Gold Corp., a Canadian mineral exploration company focused on gold and polymetallic deposits, has closed the second and final tranche of a non-brokered private placement. The tranche raised additional gross proceeds of C$631,275, taking the offering's aggregate gross proceeds, combined with a first tranche that closed October 19, 2026, to C$2,077,461.49. The release states the offering remains subject to final acceptance by the Canadian Securities Exchange. The final tranche was split between two unit types. The company issued 6,635,000 non-flow-through units at C$0.065 per unit, for gross proceeds of C$431,275, and 2,500,000 flow-through units at C$0.08 per unit, for gross proceeds of C$200,000. Flow-through units carry tax deductions the company renounces to the subscriber; non-flow-through units do not. Each non-flow-through unit consists of one common share and one-half of a warrant, with each whole warrant exercisable at C$0.12 for 24 months. Each flow-through unit consists of one flow-through common share and one-half of a warrant, with each whole warrant exercisable at C$0.15 for 24 months. The company paid aggregate cash finder's fees of C$45,042 and issued 652,800 non-transferable finder warrants, exercisable between C$0.065 and C$0.08, in connection with the offering. All securities issued in the final tranche are subject to a statutory hold period expiring March 1, 2027. Net proceeds from the flow-through portion are earmarked for eligible Canadian exploration expenses that qualify as flow-through mining expenditures, which the company will renounce to subscribers effective December 31, 2026. Chief executive Darcy Christian called the financing the largest in the company's history, citing continued support from new and returning investors. Following the close, the company had 129,888,470 common shares outstanding. The release describes the company's flagship assets as 100%-owned claims in the Dryden area of Ontario, plus an optioned Icefield claim package in British Columbia.

item.title: Goliath Resources raises C$9.8 million without issuing a single warrant
item.description: The non-brokered flow-through placement, still subject to final TSX Venture Exchange approval, funds exploration at the Golddigger-Surebet gold project in BC's Golden Triangle.
item.content:encoded: Goliath Resources Limited, an explorer of precious-metals projects in the Golden Triangle of northwestern British Columbia, has closed a non-brokered private placement for gross proceeds of C$9,800,000. The company issued 6,057,000 flow-through common shares at a price of C$1.62 per share. No warrants were attached to the units, and the company paid no finder's fees or commissions in connection with the offering. The shares were issued as flow-through shares, which qualify under subsection 66(15) of Canada's Income Tax Act. That designation lets the company renounce the associated tax deductions for qualifying exploration expenditures to the subscribers who bought the shares, rather than claiming those deductions itself — a structure used to attract investors to exploration-stage mining financings. Goliath said the funds will go toward Canadian exploration expenses and flow-through mining expenditures on its Golddigger-Surebet Gold Project. The qualifying expenditures must be incurred by December 31, 2027, and the associated tax deductions renounced to subscribers by December 31, 2026. The offering remains subject to final acceptance by the TSX Venture Exchange, the release states. The shares issued are subject to a statutory four-month hold period expiring March 1, 2027, under applicable Canadian securities law. Chief executive Roger Rosmus said the financing is "an insurance policy that further enhances our strong balance sheet and puts us in a stronger position, with ~C$27.5M in cash going into 2027 and our planned exploration drill program." The company describes its projects as sitting in "high quality geological settings and geopolitical safe jurisdictions amenable to mining in Canada." In 2026 it completed a fully funded 48,443-metre drill program on the Golddigger-Surebet project, for which assays are pending on 55 holes, following a 64,364-metre program in 2025.

item.title: US offers Audi tariff relief to keep its $4-billion Georgia plant
item.description: Audi wants its 15% tariff on EU imports cut to 7.5%; the Commerce Department is expected to settle near 10% to secure roughly 4,500 jobs.
item.content:encoded: The Trump administration has promised tariff relief to Audi to help secure the automaker's $4 billion assembly plant in Georgia, two sources briefed on the discussions told Reuters. The sources said US officials told Audi executives the government plans to offer a broader tariff relief program for automakers making significant investments in US production. Audi has pushed Washington to cut the 15% tariff it currently pays on vehicles imported from the European Union to 7.5%. The sources said the Commerce Department was expected to agree to a rate of around 10% instead. The plant is expected to assemble 200,000 SUVs a year and create approximately 4,500 jobs, according to the reporting. Construction is due to begin next year, with production starting in the early 2030s. Audi has said tariffs on autos, steel, aluminum and parts cost it roughly €1.2 billion ($1.4 billion) last year. The company currently imports every vehicle it sells in the US market from factories in Europe or Mexico, which is what exposes it fully to the tariff rate rather than partially. Audi chief executive Gernot Doellner said the Georgia investment decision followed "many months of careful planning and intense negotiations," adding, "If the American president invites you, you accept the invitation." The Commerce Department did not immediately comment, and Audi declined comment on the tariff discussions. The reporting cites two anonymous sources for the substance of the talks, plus Doellner's own public statement and earlier reporting from the Wall Street Journal. Neither Audi nor the Commerce Department has confirmed the specific 10% figure the sources attribute to the department. None of the venture-listed names the bulletin tracks under its tariffs and trade theme traded today. With no trading to measure, there is no group move to report, and the bulletin names none of them — a thin day for the theme, not a judgment on it.

item.title: SK Hynix and Samsung tumble as Intel's weak outlook spooks chip investors
item.description: Disappointing US earnings from Intel, Amazon and Alphabet triggered a broad selloff in Asian chipmakers and tech suppliers on Friday.
item.content:encoded: Technology and chip-supplier stocks fell heavily across Asian markets on Friday, with South Korea's chip heavyweights among the hardest hit. Samsung Electronics fell 5.9% and SK Hynix 8.3%. In Japan, Murata Manufacturing dropped 11%, Advantest fell 5.8%, Tokyo Electron fell more than 5%, and SoftBank Group fell nearly 7%. Taiwan's TSMC slipped 1.8% and Foxconn 3%, according to Investing.com. The selloff followed an over 20% plunge in Intel's share price after the company gave weak fourth-quarter guidance. Intel cited rising component costs and softer consumer demand weighing on its personal-computer business. Amazon added to the pressure after missing both revenue and profit estimates for its most recent quarter, with the company's cash flow deteriorating further. Alphabet's results earlier in the week had already unsettled investors, raising questions about the returns big technology companies are getting on their artificial-intelligence spending. Investing.com reported that the moves reflect mounting doubts that the money being poured into AI infrastructure will be profitable in the long term, prompting a rotation out of high-valuation technology names and into more defensive sectors of the market. Japanese equities faced an added source of pressure: the Bank of Japan signalled it may raise interest rates further and said it would increase its sales of exchange-traded funds, both of which weighed directly on Tokyo-listed shares. On the TSX Venture Exchange, the bulletin tracks three listed venture names under a semiconductor theme. Two traded today, one higher and none lower, for a median move of +2.08% against a decline of 1.47% for the S&P/TSX Venture Composite — a spread of 3.55 percentage points. Sparq Systems Inc. (TSXV: SPRQ), whose sector label is Electrical Equipment & Parts, rose 4.17% to C$1 on roughly C$71,641 of dollar volume. Wi2Wi Corporation (TSXV: YTY), whose sector label is Communication Equipment, was unchanged at C$0.125 on roughly C$62,475 of dollar volume. Both moves fell on the same day as the Asian chip selloff; nothing in the record connects one to the other.

item.title: First Lithium Minerals raises $1.44 million across a LIFE offering and placement
item.description: The financing combined a Listed Issuer Financing Exemption offering with a private placement, pricing units from 11 to 15 cents to fund exploration in Chile and Ontario.
item.content:encoded: First Lithium Minerals Corp. (CSE: FLM, OTC Pink: FLMCF, FSE: X28) explores for lithium and other alkali metals at the Salar de Ascotan in northern Chile, and for gold and critical metals at the Lidstone project in northwestern Ontario. The company said on October 29 that it has closed the second tranche of its Listed Issuer Financing Exemption, or LIFE, offering together with a concurrent private placement, for combined gross proceeds of $1,442,144. The LIFE tranche raised $597,345 through 2,466,773 non-flow-through units at $0.11 per unit and 2,173,333 flow-through units at $0.15 per unit. A Listed Issuer Financing Exemption lets a company already listed on an exchange sell securities to the public without a prospectus, provided it meets disclosure conditions set by securities regulators. The concurrent private placement raised a further $844,840 through 7,680,363 units at $0.11 per unit. Every unit across both offerings — LIFE and private placement alike — carries one-half of a common share purchase warrant, with a whole warrant exercisable at $0.18 per share for three years from closing. The private placement units are subject to the standard statutory hold period of four months and one day from closing. The LIFE Offering units, consistent with the exemption's design, carry no such hold and are freely tradeable once issued. First Lithium paid cash finder's fees of $23,908 plus 220,542 finder's warrants at $0.11 in connection with the LIFE tranche, and $33,387 in cash plus 337,702 finder's warrants in connection with the private placement. The company said net proceeds will go toward exploration activities at its Chile and Ontario projects, along with general corporate purposes and working capital. The release, filed through Newsfile Corp. from Toronto, did not break out how the proceeds will be divided between the two projects.

item.title: Fuse Battery Metals closes $644,560 private placement at five cents a unit
item.description: The non-brokered deal priced units at five cents each, with insiders taking part and the financing still subject to TSX Venture Exchange approval.
item.content:encoded: Fuse Battery Metals Inc. (TSXV: FUSE, OTC: FSBMF, FRA: 43W3) is a Canadian exploration company focused on metals used in battery manufacturing, including cobalt properties near Cobalt, Ontario. The company said on October 29 that it has closed a non-brokered private placement of 12,891,200 units at $0.05 per unit, for gross proceeds of $644,560. Each unit consists of one common share and one common share purchase warrant, with each warrant exercisable at $0.05 per share for five years from closing. Insiders of the company subscribed for 272,040 of the units in the placement, representing gross proceeds of $13,602. In connection with the financing, Fuse issued 30,000 common shares at a deemed value of $0.05 per share as a finder's fee. All securities issued under the private placement, including the finder's shares, are subject to a statutory hold period expiring March 2, 2027 under applicable Canadian securities laws. The private placement remains subject to final acceptance by the TSX Venture Exchange. Fuse said it intends to use the proceeds to pursue strategic acquisition opportunities, evaluate potential transactions, and support its ongoing corporate operations, working capital requirements and future business initiatives. The release noted that more than CAD$25 million has been spent to date — stated in 2020 dollars, inflation-adjusted — on the company's Teledyne Property, one of the cobalt holdings the financing is intended to support alongside the company's other corporate purposes. Beyond the financing terms and the brief reference to the Teledyne Property, the release gave no further operational update — no drill results, property description or revised budget — so this entry is limited to what the release discloses.

item.title: DoorDash offers $65 a share, valuing Instacart at about $17 billion
item.description: The cash-and-stock bid is a 26% premium to Instacart's October 22 closing price, with the deal targeted to close by the end of 2027 or the first half of 2028.
item.content:encoded: DoorDash has agreed to acquire Instacart, which operates under the legal name Maplebear Inc., in a deal that values the grocery-delivery company at approximately $17 billion. Instacart shareholders will be able to elect one of three forms of consideration for each share held: $65.00 in cash, 0.3372 of a DoorDash share, or a combination of $48.75 in cash and 0.0843 of a DoorDash share. The stock portion of the total consideration is capped at 25% of the deal's aggregate value, with proration mechanics built in should stock elections be oversubscribed. The per-share price represents a 26% premium to Instacart's closing stock price on October 22, 2026, according to the companies' release. Instacart's board of directors unanimously approved the transaction, and shareholders holding approximately 19% of the company's outstanding shares have already agreed to vote in favour of the deal. DoorDash said it intends to fund the cash portion of the deal using cash on hand together with proceeds from new debt, and has arranged a 364-day bridge loan facility from JPMorgan Chase. The company said the transaction carries no financing condition and that it is targeting investment-grade credit ratings. DoorDash said the combination is expected to generate more than $500 million in annual synergies within several years of closing. Completion is expected by the end of 2027 or in the first half of 2028. The deal still requires Instacart shareholder approval, clearance under the Hart-Scott-Rodino antitrust act in the United States, and regulatory approvals in Canada and Israel, along with other customary closing conditions. item.title: Teck Resources' profit jumps to $1.59 billion on copper, zinc prices
item.description: The gain from $281 million a year earlier comes as a steelworkers' strike cuts output at the company's Highland Valley Copper mine.
item.content:encoded: Teck Resources reported third-quarter profit attributable to shareholders of $1.59 billion, or $3.24 per diluted share, compared with $281 million, or 57 cents per diluted share, in the same quarter of 2025. On an adjusted basis, the company reported $1.88 per diluted share, against 76 cents adjusted a year earlier. Revenue for the quarter rose to $4.52 billion from $3.39 billion a year earlier. The company attributed the improvement in both revenue and profit to higher prices for copper and zinc, though it did not disclose specific average realized prices for either metal. Teck's shares, which trade on the Toronto Stock Exchange under the symbol TECK-B, were quoted at $89.22, up 1.27%, as of the article's publication. Separately, approximately 1,200 members of the United Steelworkers began a strike at Teck's Highland Valley Copper mine, near Logan Lake, British Columbia, over the weekend. The mine is continuing to operate at reduced capacity during the job action. Teck said the impact of the strike on production will depend on how long it lasts, without giving a specific production estimate or timeline for resolution. On the venture boards, the copper theme comprises 55 listed venture names. Thirty-nine traded today, seven higher and 22 lower, for a median move of -1.20% against a decline of -1.47% for the S&P/TSX Venture Composite — a spread of 0.27 percentage points on the day. Among names that cleared the board's liquidity floor, Xxix Metal Corp, in the theme on its sector label of Copper, fell 10.34% to $0.13; Coyote Copper Mines, whose registered name contains the word copper, fell 8.33% to $0.33; Canadian Copper, also named for the metal, rose 5.77% to $0.55; Copper Giant Resources fell 5.00% to $0.95; and Super Copper rose 4.44% to $0.47. Teck's results and the day's moves among the venture copper names fall on the same trading day. Nothing in either disclosure connects one to the other.

item.title: Aeon Strategies' crypto audit delay pushes its filing to December 31
item.description: The CSE-listed company has applied for a management cease-trade order to avoid a broader halt while its auditor works through complex crypto-related holdings.
item.content:encoded: Aeon Strategies Ltd. (CSE: AEON, OTCQB: CLDVF, FSE: WQ40), formerly known as Cloud3 Ventures Inc., has updated its timeline for filing annual financial statements for the year ended June 30, 2026. The company now expects to file its audited annual filings, management's discussion and analysis and the related CEO and CFO certifications on or before December 31, 2026 — nearly a month later than the December 4, 2026 date it had previously disclosed. The company's auditor, Davidson & Company LLP, told Aeon that the delay is due to two factors: limited availability on the auditor's side, and the additional time required to complete audit procedures relating to the company's crypto-related investments, which the release says are more complex to audit than in prior years. To manage the consequences of the late filing, Aeon has applied to its principal regulator for a management cease trade order. If granted, an MCTO would prohibit only the company's chief executive officer and chief financial officer from trading in Aeon's securities until the annual filings are submitted — leaving ordinary shareholders free to continue trading. The release states that if the management cease trade order is not granted, securities regulators may instead issue a general cease trade order prohibiting all trading in Aeon's securities, a broader measure that would affect every shareholder rather than only its two senior officers. Until the annual filings are complete, Aeon is required to issue a default status report every two weeks by news release, under the continuous disclosure provisions of National Policy 12-203 covering defaulting reporting issuers. For investors, the distinction matters: an MCTO limits only who can trade, not whether the stock keeps trading at all, while a general cease trade order would stop every shareholder from buying or selling until the annual filings catch up. Aeon's application for the narrower order is still pending regulatory approval.

item.title: Steadright's insiders are expected to buy most of the second tranche
item.description: Insiders already took 1,100,000 units of Steadright's first tranche at $0.10, and the company expects them to take most of the rest.
item.content:encoded: Steadright Critical Minerals Inc. (CSE: SCM) has closed the first tranche of a non-brokered private placement, raising $530,000 at a price of $0.10 per unit. The closing is the first of two tranches in an offering the company has now upsized to a total of $900,000. Company insiders subscribed for 1,100,000 of the units sold in this first tranche, at the same $0.10 price offered to other subscribers. The company said it expects insiders to take up most or all of the units remaining in the second and final tranche, which it expects to close within the next week. Each unit sold in the placement consists of one common share and one common share purchase warrant. Each whole warrant entitles its holder to purchase one additional common share at $0.16 for a period of twenty-four months from closing. The securities issued in the first tranche are subject to a hold period of four months and one day. The private placement overall was upsized by $100,000 to its current $900,000 total, up to 9,000,000 units in aggregate across both tranches. Steadright paid finder's fees of $18,600 on 3,100,000 of the units sold in the first tranche, along with a finder's fee warrant equal to 6% of the gross proceeds. The release does not name the recipient, referring only to "eligible parties" under applicable securities laws. The company describes itself as a mineral exploration business focused on Morocco's critical mineral space, where it holds exposure through a Moroccan entity, NSM Capital Sarl, to more than 192 square kilometres of claims covering the TitanBeach Titanium Project and the Copper Valley Project, plus a binding memorandum of understanding for the historic Goundafa Mine. Proceeds from the placement are earmarked for general working capital, corporate purposes and potential strategic initiatives, and the offering remains subject to approval from the Canadian Securities Exchange.

item.title: SK Hynix is handing shareholders $75 billion after a sevenfold profit jump
item.description: The chipmaker's operating profit rose more than sevenfold to 83.3 trillion won as AI-driven demand for memory chips sold out capacity into 2029.
item.content:encoded: SK Hynix said on Tuesday it will return approximately 100 trillion won, or about $75 billion, to shareholders this year, after third-quarter operating profit surged more than sevenfold to 83.3 trillion won from 11.4 trillion won a year earlier. Quarterly revenue rose 328% to 104.6 trillion won. The company is the world's largest maker of high-bandwidth memory chips used in artificial-intelligence data centres. The shareholder return is split between roughly 30 trillion won in cash dividends and 60 trillion won in share repurchases and cancellations, the latter figure including the 40 trillion won in buybacks the company had already announced in August. Shares in SK Hynix rose as much as 9.4% following the announcement. Chief financial officer Kim Woo-hyun said the company expects AI investment momentum to continue, with customers' AI spending translating into broader adoption of AI services and tangible business results. Analyst Ryu Young-ho of NH Investment & Securities said the results had eased many of the market's concerns, with earnings coming in ahead of expectations. SK Hynix said it has sold out its high-bandwidth memory and DRAM chip production through 2029 and has signed long-term supply agreements with 14 major customers covering more than half of its planned 2027-2028 production capacity. The company said it expects memory-chip demand to continue exceeding supply through 2030. On the venture boards, the read-through is semiconductors — the theme a chipmaker's results fall into on this desk's sector mapping. The theme comprises three listed venture names; three traded today, two higher and one lower, for a median move of +3.09%, against +1.60% for the S&P/TSX Venture Composite, a spread of 1.49 percentage points in the theme's favour. None of the three names cleared the C$25,000 day-volume floor this desk requires before naming a security on a given day's move, so none is named here. A percentage change on a stock that prints without real volume behind it is a stale quote, not a market move, and this desk does not report it as one. The coincidence of SK Hynix's results and the theme's move establishes nothing beyond timing. Nothing here attributes the venture names' trading to SK Hynix, and no causal link should be inferred from the two falling on the same day.

item.title: Rush Gold adds two Nevada gold properties and a 40-year mining veteran as chairman
item.description: The CSE-listed junior also closed a second placement tranche for $1,030,500 as it builds out its Walker Lane Trend portfolio.
item.content:encoded: Rush Gold Corp. (CSE: RGN, FSE: B6H) said it has completed the acquisition of Landy Investments Ltd., through which the company gained the rights to two mineral properties in Nevada's Walker Lane Trend: the Hollow North-South project and the Douglas Canyon project. The release does not state the consideration paid for Landy Investments — no share issuance or cash amount is disclosed for the transaction. Hollow North-South, a copper-gold property, is located about 15 kilometres east of Yerington, Nevada, on 109 claims on land managed by the U.S. Bureau of Land Management. Rush Gold holds an 80% interest in the project, which the company said complements its existing Skylight and Legal Tender projects. Douglas Canyon, a gold-antimony property, is located about 80 kilometres northwest of Tonopah, Nevada, and covers 138 claims on BLM land. The release gives no interest percentage for Douglas Canyon, unlike the 80% stake disclosed for Hollow North-South, and does not state the terms on which Rush Gold acquired its rights to the property. Rush Gold also appointed Andy Tudor as chairman. The company described Tudor as a geologist and mining executive with more than 40 years of experience across the mineral exploration and mining sectors. The release gives no further biographical detail. Separately, the company closed the second tranche of a non-brokered private placement, issuing 10,305,000 shares for gross proceeds of $1,030,500. The release does not disclose a price per share, warrant terms, or a closing date for the tranche, and does not name an agent or finder. The company also said it has engaged CPS Capital Group and EuroSwiss Capital Partners on advisory, communications and marketing work intended to strengthen market awareness. Rush Gold said planned exploration activity across its Nevada projects includes geological mapping, geochemical sampling, geophysics and drill testing, without giving a timeline for any of the programs.

item.title: Edison Lithium is raising up to $1.9 million at 7 cents a unit

item.title: Argentum AI is negotiating $5 billion in debt to buy more AI chips
item.description: The Chicago-based neocloud, which already has $12 billion in contracted revenue, wants the financing to lease chips to customers without investment-grade credit.
item.content:encoded: Argentum AI, a Chicago-based cloud computing company backed by Super Micro, is in talks with a major private credit firm for a $5 billion financing deal, Reuters reported on Tuesday, citing two people familiar with the matter. The debt would fund additional AI chips for a data centre Argentum is building in Poland with DL Invest Group. The financing is intended for chips leased to customers that do not carry investment-grade credit ratings, according to the sources. Argentum was founded in 2025 by chief executive Andrew Sobko and describes itself as an independent, institutional-grade AI cloud platform focused on deploying large-scale GPU infrastructure for enterprise AI. Argentum has more than $12 billion in contracted revenue, Reuters reported. In May, the company signed roughly a $2.5 billion agreement with cloud-gaming firm Boosteroid and DL Invest Group for a 300-megawatt data centre facility. The talks come a day after SpaceX secured $40 billion in debt financing for chips from an affiliate of Apollo Global Management, as financing has tightened for "neoclouds" — firms that rent out AI computing power. Elon Musk said "debt markets have almost entirely shut off access to money for companies without substantial revenue independent of AI data centers," and predicted significant consolidation among the sector's more than 200 competitors. On the venture boards, the read-through is artificial intelligence and data centres. The theme comprises 29 listed venture names; 17 traded today, 5 higher and 6 lower, for a median move of +0.00%, against +1.60% for the S&P/TSX Venture Composite — a spread of 1.60 percentage points against the theme. (CSE: AIML) was unchanged at CAD0.04, and is in the theme because its registered name contains "ai." item.title: A proxy adviser is telling H&R REIT investors to reject a $3.4-billion buyout
item.description: ISS cited concerns about the sale process and an insider-linked side deal ahead of the November 13 unitholder vote on the GO Residential takeover.
item.content:encoded: Proxy adviser Institutional Shareholder Services is recommending that unitholders of H&R Real Estate Investment Trust vote against the trust's proposed $3.4-billion acquisition by GO Residential Real Estate Investment Trust, a deal announced in August. Under its terms, H&R unitholders would receive $4.28 in cash plus 0.5688 of a GO unit for every H&R unit they hold. The vote is scheduled for November 13. ISS's recommendation cited concerns over the sale process, conflicts of interest, the logic of the deal and whether disinterested unitholders are capturing fair value relative to insiders. The adviser pointed to a related transaction in which a company controlled by H&R chief executive Tom Hofstedter would acquire $1.98 billion of properties, at book value, for $1.56 billion — different consideration than other unitholders are receiving in the main transaction. Several institutional investors have already said publicly they intend to vote against the deal, including RBC Global Asset Management, Mill Pond Capital and Sandpiper Group. Rival proxy adviser Glass Lewis is expected to publish its own recommendation in the coming week. GO Residential's unit price has declined since the deal was announced, reducing the value of the consideration H&R unitholders would receive. H&R faces a $102-million termination fee if the transaction does not proceed. GO Residential Real Estate Investment Trust owns luxury apartments in New York. As part of the transaction, GO would issue 134.2 million of its own units to help fund the acquisition of $1.8 billion of residential properties. On the venture boards, the read-through is real estate — the sector theme a REIT takeover falls into on this desk's mapping. The theme comprises 12 listed venture names; 3 traded today, 1 higher and 1 lower, for a median move of +0.00%, against +1.60% for the S&P/TSX Venture Composite — a spread of 1.60 percentage points against the theme. None of the three names that traded cleared the C$25,000 day-volume floor this desk requires before naming a security, so none is named here. The coincidence of the ISS recommendation and the theme's flat median move establishes nothing beyond timing, and no causal link should be inferred.

item.title: Red Canyon Resources closes $745,000 flow-through raise for BC critical minerals
item.description: The non-brokered placement issued 3,725,000 flow-through units at $0.20 each, with half-warrants exercisable at $0.30 for 18 months.
item.content:encoded: Red Canyon Resources Ltd. (CSE: REDC) (OTCQB: REDRF) (Frankfurt: I91) has closed a non-brokered flow-through private placement for gross proceeds of $745,000. The offering consisted of 3,725,000 flow-through units priced at $0.20 each. Each FT Unit comprised one flow-through common share and one-half of one common share purchase warrant, with each whole warrant exercisable into one common share at $0.30 for an 18-month term. A flow-through share lets the company renounce the associated Canadian exploration expenses to the subscriber, who can then claim them against their own income for tax purposes — which is why flow-through financings are typically priced at a premium to a company's regular shares. Red Canyon's release did not state whether this placement carried that kind of premium. The company said the proceeds qualify as flow-through critical mineral mining expenditures and are earmarked for exploration on its Kendal and Osiris projects and other eligible British Columbia properties. The expenditure deadline is December 31, 2027, and the related renunciation of the expenses to subscribers is effective December 31, 2026, the company said. Red Canyon paid finder's fees of $24,025 in connection with the offering. Insiders of the company purchased 937,500 of the flow-through units, the release said, without further detail on which insiders participated or in what amounts individually. All securities issued under the offering — the flow-through shares and the warrants — are restricted from trading until February 27, 2027. The offering closed October 26, 2026. Red Canyon is a Vancouver-based company exploring in British Columbia, trading on the CSE under REDC, on the OTCQB under REDRF, and in Frankfurt under I91. The release did not disclose the current size of the company's exploration programs beyond naming the Kendal and Osiris projects as a focus for the new proceeds.

item.title: MineHub arranges $1.5 million placement, pushes warrant expiry out to 2027

A unit, in this structure, bundles a share together with the right to buy additional shares later at a fixed price — the warrant — giving subscribers upside if the stock trades above $0.55 before the warrant expires, without requiring them to pay for that right up front beyond the unit price. Alongside the new placement, MineHub is extending the expiry of warrants it issued earlier. Prior warrants covering 14,584,954 shares at an exercise price of $0.40, issued January 31, 2024, along with 625,000 warrants at $0.50 issued July 25, 2025 and 550,463 warrants at $0.50 issued August 20, 2025, all had their expiry pushed from January 31, 2027 to December 31, 2027. Closing of the offering is subject to the company's receipt of TSX Venture Exchange approval, MineHub said. No closing date was given in the release. MineHub said the proceeds are earmarked for working capital and for continuing to evaluate strategic, corporate and financial opportunities. The release gave no further detail on what those opportunities might involve.

item.title: Nvidia is putting $3 billion into Meta's largest-ever fundraising round
item.description: The chipmaker's stake deepens a partnership on Meta's Muse AI assistant, built on Nvidia hardware, as Meta boosts its planned offering to $97.5 billion.
item.content:encoded: Nvidia is investing $3 billion in Meta Platforms' equity offering, which Meta increased to $97.5 billion. Reuters reported the enlarged raise is the largest fundraising in Meta's history. Meta is raising the money as it accelerates investment in AI infrastructure, Reuters reported. The deal deepens an existing partnership on Muse, Meta's personal AI assistant, internally known as Hatch, which runs on Nvidia infrastructure. Muse can access a user's email, calendar, payments, health, shopping and smart-home applications, with users able to revoke that access at any time, according to the reporting. The companies are also exploring joint work on Nvidia's OpenShell framework and a monitoring tool called Sentry, which is intended to track AI agent behaviour, Reuters reported. Chief executive Mark Zuckerberg has described Muse as central to delivering what he calls "personal superintelligence" to Meta's users; the system is modelled on the open-source AI agent OpenClaw, according to the reporting. item.title: Anthropic files for an IPO that could be the biggest ever
item.description: The AI company could raise up to $100 billion at a valuation of $1.5 trillion to $2 trillion, even as its chief executive warns of a risk to humanity from unchecked AI.
item.content:encoded: Anthropic has filed papers for an initial public offering that could be the largest in history, the Associated Press reported. The filing sets up a Wall Street debut as soon as next month, with the company potentially raising as much as $100 billion at a valuation of $1.5 trillion to $2 trillion — topping the $86 billion raised by SpaceX's IPO in June, previously the record. Anthropic plans to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker ANT. The company was founded in 2021 by a group of former OpenAI employees, including siblings Dario Amodei, its chief executive, and Daniela Amodei, its president. It reported revenue of more than $16 billion for the first half of 2026, fourteen times the prior year's figure, according to the AP. Anthropic also reported a net loss of $80.7 billion for the period, which includes a one-time accounting charge of $72.4 billion. The company has not yet reported a profit. Its seven founders are each expected to hold about 1.4% of the company, a stake that could be worth as much as $28 billion apiece at the top of the expected valuation range, the AP reported. The founders will retain 50.1% voting control through a special class of shares, and the company has established a Long-Term Benefit Trust of independent directors with the power to appoint board members, structured to keep financial interests from overriding public-safety considerations, according to the filing as reported by the AP. Dario Amodei has separately argued, in a post on his website, for slowing development of the most advanced AI models, warning that without an industry slowdown, AI could let loose "a swarm of agents" that could "take over the entire internet" within six to 12 months, the AP reported. The space theme on this publication's venture boards comprises two listed names; neither cleared the C$25,000 daily-volume floor this publication requires before naming a security today. No junior move is therefore reported alongside Anthropic's filing, and no names are given.

item.title: US and Canada edge toward a deal to ease steel and auto tariffs
item.description: Talks center on Section 232 duties of up to 50% on steel and 25% on autos, with Canadian sources saying a deal before the November 3 elections is possible but would likely be narrower in scope.
item.content:encoded: The United States and Canada are working on a deal to ease U.S. tariffs on Canadian steel and autos, Reuters reported, citing sources briefed on the talks. The negotiations aim to repair relations that soured after broader trade talks broke down in August, and focus on Section 232 duties — a US trade-law provision under which Washington has imposed tariffs of up to 50% on Canadian steel and 25% on Canadian autos. Trump has said he intends to raise the Canadian steel tariff to 50% from its current level starting January 1, 2027, absent a deal. He predicted at a political rally on Sunday that the trade dispute would be resolved "soon," without giving specifics, Reuters reported. Because Section 232 tariffs are administered by the US Commerce Department, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is at the center of the talks rather than the Office of the US Trade Representative, and Reuters reported he has been in regular contact with Canada's Dominic LeBlanc, the minister handling the file for Ottawa. A spokesperson for LeBlanc described the discussions as "constructive dialogue" on "a range of priorities." Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said there had been a "slight intensification" in talks, adding that "to the extent any progress has been made, it's because the US is coming closer to our position." One Canadian source briefed on the negotiations told Reuters that a deal was possible before the November 3 US midterm elections. A separate Canadian industry source told Reuters that any deal was likely to be "a narrowed deal" if it happens. Trump signed an order on Friday removing the 50% tariff on some Canadian agricultural and forestry products, Reuters reported. This publication's tariffs theme produced no trading today, so there is no junior read-through to set alongside the talks: no venture name in the theme traded, leaving no group measure and no names to report, unlike the artificial-intelligence and space themes tracked elsewhere in this issue.

item.title: Ovintiv to acquire Logan Energy for C$1.26 billion
item.description: The all-cash deal adds about 266,000 net acres and 20,000 barrels of oil equivalent a day in the Montney's oil window, with closing expected early in 2027.
item.content:encoded: Ovintiv Inc. (NYSE:OVV, TSX:OVV) said it has agreed to acquire Logan Energy Corp. (TSXV:LGN) in an all-cash transaction. Logan shareholders will receive C$1.40 per share, for total consideration of approximately $890 million, or C$1.26 billion, including the assumption of Logan's net debt. The agreement was announced October 26, 2026, and the boards of both companies have unanimously approved it. The transaction brings Ovintiv roughly 266,000 net acres in the oil-rich window of the Montney formation, along with about 20,000 barrels of oil equivalent a day of current production, the release said. Ovintiv said the acreage carries approximately 420 net oil well locations drilled on a 10,000-foot equivalent lateral basis, including about 220 it classifies as premium return locations, at an average cost of $1.5 million per location, and roughly 200 as upside locations. The release said Logan's assets also include about 60,000 net acres with exposure to the Duvernay shale, two new oil batteries at Simonette with combined capacity of 24,000 barrels of oil a day, and interests in two natural gas processing facilities. These assets are included within the total consideration of approximately $890 million, or C$1.26 billion, that Ovintiv has agreed to pay, including the assumption of Logan's net debt. Ovintiv said the acquisition is expected to be accretive to its 2027 Non-GAAP Cash Flow per Share by approximately 5% and to its Non-GAAP Free Cash Flow per Share by approximately 3%. The company also said it expects annual cost synergies of about $60 million and capital savings of more than $2 million per well, and that its net debt is expected to be below $4 billion following the transaction's close. Ovintiv President and CEO Brendan McCracken said: "This bolt-on transaction delivers value for our shareholders by adding high margin oil and condensate production and infrastructure, utilizing our operational advantage to drive significant synergies, and adding to our already deep drilling inventory and future growth optionality." The release's own headline described the transaction as unlocking 'incremental profitability,' providing 'additional oil growth optionality' and adding to 'premium return drilling inventory.' Completion is expected early in the first quarter of 2027, subject to Logan shareholder approval, court approval, customary regulatory approvals and other customary closing conditions, the release said. RBC Capital Markets is acting as exclusive financial advisor to Ovintiv on the transaction, with Blake, Cassels & Graydon LLP and Paul, Weiss, Rifkind, Wharton & Garrison LLP serving as Ovintiv's legal advisors. Ovintiv said its targeted shareholder returns are unchanged, with at least 60% of 2026 Non-GAAP Free Cash Flow expected to be returned to shareholders.

item.title: MetroCity Bankshares reports $24.3 million third-quarter net income

item.content:encoded: MetroCity Bankshares, Inc. (NASDAQ: MCBS), the Atlanta-based holding company for Metro City Bank, reported net income of $24.3 million, or $0.84 per diluted share, for the third quarter of 2026 ended September 30, 2026, according to its earnings release dated October 23, 2026. Dividends paid per share for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 totaled $0.87, compared with $0.71 for the same period in 2025. The release names Farid Tan as President and Interim Chief Financial Officer; no other executive is quoted. The release includes cautionary language stating that actual results could differ from any forward-looking statements due to factors including economic and market conditions, changes in interest rates, competitive pressures in the banking industry, and regulatory developments. item.title: Manufacturing sales edged up 0.1 percent in September
item.description: Statistics Canada's advance estimate points to gains led by petroleum and coal products and aerospace, with final figures due November 13.
item.content:encoded: Statistics Canada released an advance indicator on October 23, 2026 estimating that total manufacturing sales edged up 0.1% in September 2026. The agency said the largest increases were in the petroleum and coal product subsector and the aerospace product and parts industry group. The release gives no specific percentage change for either of those two groups, and no figures for any other subsector. Statistics Canada said the advance estimate is based on a weighted response rate of 71.3%, compared with an average final response rate of 92.4% over the preceding 12 months — a lower response rate that the agency says carries more risk of revision than a final estimate. The agency's official manufacturing sales figures for September 2026 are scheduled for release on November 13, 2026. The disclosure in this advance release is limited to the single aggregate figure, the two named industry groups, and the response-rate caveat; no further detail or commentary is given.

item.title: GOAT Industries to acquire casino contract revenues from Epoxy AI
item.description: The deal, paid in 11,377,600 GOAT shares at C$0.25 each, covers rights to six U.S. tribal casino and sportsbook contracts.
item.content:encoded: GOAT Industries Ltd. (CSE: GOAT) said its indirect wholly owned subsidiary, Source Gaming Company, operating as BetSource, has entered into a definitive contract revenue assignment agreement dated October 20, 2026, with Epoxy AI, LLC. Under the agreement, Source Gaming will acquire customer contract revenues from Epoxy in exchange for 11,377,600 common shares of GOAT, issued at a price of C$0.25 per share. The rights being acquired cover revenues, receivables and other amounts payable under six customer contracts Epoxy holds with U.S. tribal casinos and other established casino and sports book operators. Rather than transferring the underlying contracts immediately, the agreement structures the deal as an assignment of the revenue stream from those contracts to Source Gaming. Epoxy is to formally assign the underlying customer contracts to Source Gaming within six months of closing, subject to the consent of the customers involved. Until that assignment takes place, the release said Epoxy will continue to perform its obligations under the contracts and will hold the resulting revenue in trust for Source Gaming. Completion of the transaction is subject to the satisfaction or waiver of certain conditions, including the release of applicable security interests, other necessary approvals, and acceptance by the Canadian Securities Exchange. Either party may terminate the agreement if the transaction has not closed by November 30, 2026. Separately, the release said a US$100,000 non-interest-bearing promissory note dated January 2026 remains outstanding between the companies and will survive completion of the transaction. "This Agreement marks an important step forward in delivering on the strategy we outlined to shareholders," Hank Frecon, acting chief executive of Source Gaming Company, said in the release. The release described the transaction as advancing an acquisition strategy GOAT had previously outlined to shareholders in August 2026.

(NYSE: ACA) in the S&P SmallCap 600, S&P Dow Jones Indices said, effective before the opening of trading on Wednesday, October 28, 2026. It operates as a division of S&P Global (NYSE: SPGI). item.title: Hyperliquid Strategies boosts buyback authorization to $100 million
item.description: The board extended the program's expiration from December 2026 to October 31, 2027, and said about $72 million remains available for buybacks under the enlarged authorization.
item.content:encoded: Hyperliquid Strategies Inc. (Nasdaq: PURR) said its board of directors has authorized an increase to the company's stock repurchase program, raising the total authorization to $100 million from $30 million. The board also extended the program's termination date, pushing it out to October 31, 2027, from its original expiration of December 5, 2026. The company said approximately $72 million remains available for repurchases under the expanded authorization. A share repurchase, or buyback, program authorizes a company to buy back its own outstanding stock up to a set dollar amount, rather than committing it to purchase any fixed number of shares by a set date. The release said Hyperliquid Strategies may carry out repurchases through open market transactions, privately negotiated transactions, or other methods permitted under federal securities laws, with the timing, volume and price of any purchases left to management's discretion. The company describes itself as a digital asset treasury company built around HYPE, the native token of the Hyperliquid blockchain network, aiming to give U.S. and institutional investors capital-efficient exposure to the token through staking and yield strategies. The release said the increase "reflects the Board's confidence in the Company's long-term capital strategy and provides flexibility to buy back PURR shares as part of the Company's broader treasury management framework." The company said the timing, number and value of any shares repurchased will depend on the stock price, market conditions and legal requirements, and will remain at management's discretion. It said the board may extend, suspend or discontinue the program at any time without notice, and that there is no guarantee as to how many shares will ultimately be bought back. Beyond the dollar figures, the revised expiration date and the board's general statement of rationale, the release provides no additional detail on the buyback program.

item.title: Canadian retail sales rose 1.2% in August
item.description: Statistics Canada said sales reached $74.6 billion, with gains in all nine retail subsectors and a preliminary estimate pointing to a 0.7% rise in September.
item.content:encoded: Statistics Canada said retail sales in Canada rose 1.2% to $74.6 billion in August 2026, with increases recorded across all nine retail subsectors tracked in the survey. Motor vehicle and parts dealers posted the largest gain, also up 1.2%; gasoline stations rose 1.7%; and food and beverage retailers increased 1.1%, their first gain in three months, the agency said. Core retail sales, a measure that excludes gasoline stations and motor vehicle and parts dealers, rose 1.1% in August. In volume terms, which adjust the dollar figures for price changes, sales were also up 1.2%, indicating the increase reflected a rise in the quantity of goods sold rather than price alone. Provincial results varied. Ontario led with a 2.2% increase to $28.5 billion in retail sales, and British Columbia followed with a 2.1% increase to $10.0 billion. Sales declined in six provinces and territories — Newfoundland and Labrador, Prince Edward Island, New Brunswick, Alberta, Yukon and Nunavut — by between 0.1% and 0.6%, the agency said. E-commerce sales totalled $5.6 billion in August, up 1.1% from July and accounting for 7.6% of total retail trade for the month. Statistics Canada also published an advance estimate for September 2026, suggesting retail sales rose 0.7% for the month. The agency said the estimate is preliminary, based on a survey response rate of 58.5% compared with a historical average of 86.8%, and is subject to revision. The retail sales data are seasonally adjusted and reported in current dollars, the agency said.

item.title: Lighthouse Gold upsizes private placement to $6.45 million
item.description: Lighthouse Gold increased a private placement announced the day before, citing strong investor demand, with closing expected in early November.
item.content:encoded: Lighthouse Gold Inc. (CSE: LGHT) announced on October 23, 2026 that it has increased the size of a private placement first announced October 22, 2026. item.title: Fewer young women meet activity guidelines, Statistics Canada reports
item.description: Statistics Canada's October Health Reports found that 46% of Canadian adults met weekly activity guidelines, with activity trends diverging by age and sex.
item.content:encoded: Statistics Canada published Health Reports for October 2026 on October 21, 2026, reporting that 46% of Canadian adults met the public health recommendation of at least 150 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity per week. The figures are drawn from accelerometer-measured data collected through the Canadian Health Measures Survey, which the agency said allows tracking of population-level activity trends over time, covering the period from 2007 to 2024. The agency said the share of men aged 18 to 39 meeting the recommendation held stable at 65% across that period, from 2007 to 2024. Over the same seventeen years, the share of women aged 18 to 39 meeting the recommendation declined, from 52% to 43%, according to the release. Statistics Canada did not state a reason for the divergence between the two groups. Adults aged 60 to 79 moved in the opposite direction from the youngest cohort of women: the agency reported a nine-percentage-point increase in the share meeting the recommendation for both men and women in that age group between 2007 and 2024. The release did not provide the specific starting and ending percentages for this age group, only the size of the increase. Statistics Canada said that knowing the share of adults who meet the 150-minute threshold does not tell the whole story, because it also matters how close those who fall short are to reaching it. The agency therefore also measured, for 2022 to 2024, the gap between non-compliant adults' actual activity levels and the recommended threshold. Over that 2022-to-2024 period, 34% of women aged 18 to 39 needed only 5 to 10 additional minutes of activity a day to meet the recommendation, the agency said. Among women aged 60 to 79, 50% were getting less than 10 qualifying minutes of activity a day over the same period. The release also reported that, from 2022 to 2024, approximately one-third of Canadian adults recorded at least 7,500 steps a day, with minimal differences between men and women on that measure over the period. The agency did not report a corresponding steps-based figure for 2007, so no comparable trend over time is available for step counts.

item.title: Pacific Imperial ends Brownell Lake option agreement

item.title: S&T Bancorp posts record quarterly earnings per share
item.description: The Pennsylvania bank holding company reported $38.6 million in third-quarter net income and continued its share buyback program.
item.content:encoded: S&T Bancorp, Inc. (NASDAQ: STBA), the Indiana, Pennsylvania-based holding company for S&T Bank, reported third-quarter 2026 net income of $38.6 million, up from $36.6 million in the second quarter of 2026 and $35.0 million in the third quarter of 2025. Diluted earnings per share was $1.09, which the company said represented a 6.9% increase from the prior quarter and a 19.8% increase from a year earlier, and which its own release headlined as a record. Profitability measures improved across the board: return on average assets was 1.55%, return on average equity was 10.84%, and return on average tangible shareholders' equity, a non-GAAP measure, was 14.81%. Net interest margin on a fully taxable equivalent basis expanded seven basis points from the prior quarter to 4.06%. Asset quality metrics moved favorably. Nonperforming assets decreased $3.7 million to $36.5 million, representing 0.45% of total loans plus other real estate owned. Net charge-offs totaled $2.1 million, or 0.10% of average loans. The allowance for credit losses was unchanged at $93.3 million, or 1.16% of total portfolio loans. On the balance sheet, total assets were flat at $9.9 billion. Total deposits decreased $22.2 million and total borrowings decreased $60.0 million to $215.3 million. Total portfolio loans decreased $4.4 million, which the company attributed to lower line utilization. S&T Bancorp said it has repurchased 3,169,294 shares, or 8.3% of shares outstanding, since the fourth quarter of 2025, at an average price of $42.09 per share. Approximately 35.3 million shares were outstanding at quarter-end. The company also declared a dividend of $0.37 per share. CEO Chris McComish said the results reflected "record earnings per share, record revenue and higher core profitability."

item.title: Norfolk Southern reports record quarterly revenue
item.description: The railroad posted $3.5 billion in third-quarter revenue and diluted earnings per share of $3.37, both up from a year earlier.
item.content:encoded: Norfolk Southern Corporation (NYSE: NSC) reported third-quarter 2026 results on October 22, 2026. Revenue was $3.5 billion, which the company's release described as a quarterly record, up $423 million, or 14%, from the third quarter of 2025. Income from railway operations was $1.2 billion, up $52 million, or 5%. Diluted earnings per share was $3.37, up $0.21, or 7%, from a year earlier. The operating ratio — the share of revenue consumed by operating expenses, where a lower figure indicates greater efficiency — was 67.4% for the quarter, compared with 64.6% in the third quarter of 2025. The company said volume increased 3% year over year. Norfolk Southern also reported adjusted results that it said exclude merger-related expenses and the effects of the Eastern Ohio incident. On that adjusted basis, income from railway operations was $1.2 billion, up 7% from a year earlier, with an adjusted operating ratio of 65.4%. Adjusted diluted earnings per share was $3.62, up 10% from the third quarter of 2025. CEO Mark George said: "Norfolk Southern delivered another quarter of solid execution, with record revenues, and strong earnings growth." The release described Norfolk Southern's network as spanning 22 states and moving approximately 7 million carloads annually, operating what it called the most extensive intermodal network in the eastern United States, and said rail transport helps its customers avoid approximately 15 million tons of carbon emissions each year.

item.title: Redwood AI special warrants trigger deadline penalty
item.description: Missing a 90-day filing deadline raises the units issuable under the company's $3.5 million special warrant financing by 10 percent.
item.content:encoded: Redwood AI Corp. (CSE: AIRX) (OTCQB: RDWCF) (Frankfurt: Y0N, WKN: A422EZ) said in an October 20, 2026 release that it did not meet the 90-day deadline to file a prospectus supplement qualifying the distribution of units issuable upon deemed exercise of the special warrants issued in its special warrant financing. The brokered private placement of 1,663,000 special warrants closed July 21, 2026 for aggregate gross proceeds of approximately $3.5 million, with Maxim Group LLC acting as exclusive placement agent. The 90-day deadline, which the release calls the Penalty Deadline, was set under the terms of the special warrants and an agency agreement between Redwood and Maxim dated July 16, 2026, entered into in connection with the offering. A special warrant of this kind converts into units of the company once a prospectus qualifying the underlying securities is filed, or on a backstop date if it is not; missing the filing deadline activates a penalty built into the warrant's own terms. That penalty increases the number of units issuable on deemed exercise of each special warrant from 1.00 to 1.10, for no additional consideration, the release said. Applied across the 1,663,000 special warrants outstanding, the total units issuable rises to 1,829,300 from 1,663,000, an increase of 166,300 units. Each unit comprises one common share of Redwood and one warrant exercisable at $2.48 per share for 60 months, according to the release. The units will be issued on the earlier of Redwood filing the prospectus supplement or November 22, 2026. The release does not state a revised date by which Redwood expects to file the prospectus supplement, nor does it give a reason the original deadline was missed. No further transaction step beyond the November 22, 2026 backstop date for deemed exercise is described in the release.

item.title: Noble Mineral closes Lucas Gold Project purchase

item.content:encoded: Noble Mineral Exploration Inc. (TSX-V: NOB) (FRANKFURT: NB7) (OTCQB: NLPXF) announced October 21, 2026 that it has closed the transactions under a Purchase Agreement with Canada Nickel Company Inc., under which Noble acquires the Lucas Gold Project. The transactions were previously announced in Noble's news releases dated July 13, 2026 and September 17, 2026. The company said Noble has received final acceptance from the TSX Venture Exchange for the transactions under the agreement. No further conditions or approvals are described in this announcement. It states no use of proceeds and no next procedural step beyond the exchange acceptance already obtained. Noble describes itself, in the release's standard company description, as a Canadian-based junior exploration company that holds securities in Canada Nickel Company Inc., among other listed holdings. The release lists H. Vance White, President, as the contact for further information. Taken together, the two releases Noble points to — October 21 confirming closing and exchange acceptance, and September 17 setting out the terms — mean a reader following only today's announcement sees confirmation that a previously announced acquisition has completed, without the underlying deal terms restated in the same document.

item.title: M/I Homes reports lower third-quarter revenue, profit
item.description: The homebuilder's net income fell to $66.6 million on revenue of $1.076 billion as new contracts and deliveries each declined 2% from a year earlier.
item.content:encoded: M/I Homes, Inc. (NYSE: MHO), the Columbus, Ohio-based homebuilder marking its 50th anniversary in 2026, reported results for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026. Third-quarter revenue was $1.076 billion, down 5% from $1.132 billion a year earlier. Net income was $66.6 million, or $2.56 per diluted share, against $106.5 million, or $3.92 per share, in the third quarter of 2025. Pre-tax income for the quarter was $86.9 million, down 38% from $139.8 million, a decline the company tied in part to $4.7 million of pre-tax inventory charges taken in the quarter, against $8.9 million for the first nine months. Gross margin was 20.9% as reported and 21.3% excluding the inventory charges. New contracts for the quarter fell 2% to 1,861 and homes delivered fell 2% to 2,241, at an average closing price of $460,000, with a cancellation rate of 12%. For the nine months, homes delivered fell 4% to 6,361 while new contracts rose 5% to 6,598, against 6,620 and 6,278, respectively, a year earlier. The company's backlog stood at 2,046 homes at September 30, 2026, down 7% from a year earlier, with a sales value of $1.103 billion, down 9%, and an average sales price of $539,000. M/I Homes operated 246 communities at quarter-end, up from 233 a year earlier. The company reported shareholders' equity of $3.3 billion and book value of $130 per share, both company records, along with $621 million of cash and equivalents, a homebuilding debt-to-capital ratio of 18%, a net debt-to-capital ratio of 2%, and zero borrowings outstanding on its $900 million credit facility. M/I Homes repurchased $50 million of its shares during the quarter. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, pre-tax income was $280.6 million, against $446.0 million a year earlier, and net income was $213.5 million, or $8.14 per diluted share, against $339.0 million, or $12.32 per share, in the first nine months of 2025. Chief executive Robert H. Schottenstein said the quarter's results 'reflect increasingly difficult market conditions, including higher mortgage interest rates, weaker demand and growing economic uncertainty,' adding that the company is 'well positioned to manage through this current cycle given the strength of our balance sheet, low debt levels, diverse product offerings and well-located communities.' The company said it will hold a conference call on October 21, 2026 at 10:30 a.m. ET to discuss the results. The release includes no forward guidance for the fourth quarter or full year beyond the comments attributed to Schottenstein.
